The cubic polynomial is \(x^{3} - \frac{n}{6}x^{2} + (n - 11)x - 400\). Its roots are \(\alpha^{2}, \beta^{2}, \gamma^{2}\). By Vieta,
\[
\alpha^{2}+\beta^{2}+\gamma^{2}=\frac{n}{6},\qquad
\alpha^{2}\beta^{2}+\beta^{2}\gamma^{2}+\gamma^{2}\alpha^{2}=n-11,\qquad
\alpha^{2}\beta^{2}\gamma^{2}=400.
\]
Let \(r=\alpha^{2}, s=\beta^{2}, t=\gamma^{2}\). The possible sums \(S=\alpha+\beta+\gamma\) are obtained by choosing signs for the square roots: \(S=\varepsilon_{1}\sqrt{r}+\varepsilon_{2}\sqrt{s}+\varepsilon_{3}\sqrt{t}\) with \(\varepsilon_i=\pm1\). There are \(8\) such sums. They are distinct unless there is a nontrivial linear relation among \(\sqrt{r},\sqrt{s},\sqrt{t}\) with coefficients in \(\{-1,0,1\}\). For exactly seven distinct sums, exactly two sign patterns must coincide, which occurs if and only if (after appropriate sign choices) \(\sqrt{t}=\sqrt{r}\pm\sqrt{s}\) (or a permutation). Squaring gives \(t=r+s\pm2\sqrt{rs}\), i.e., \((t-r-s)^2=4rs\). For a permutation of the roots, this condition leads (using Vieta) to
\[
4t^{3}-4S_{1}t^{2}+S_{1}^{2}t-4P=0,
\]
where \(S_{1}=r+s+t=n/6\), \(S_{2}=rs+st+tr=n-11\), \(P=rst=400\). Substituting the cubic relation \(t^{3}=S_{1}t^{2}-S_{2}t+P\) yields
\[
t(S_{1}^{2}-4S_{2})=0.
\]
Since \(t\neq0\) (product \(400\)), we must have \(S_{1}^{2}=4S_{2}\). Hence
\[
\left(\frac{n}{6}\right)^{2}=4(n-11)\;\Longrightarrow\; n^{2}=144n-1584\;\Longrightarrow\; n^{2}-144n+1584=0.
\]
Solving gives \(n=12\) or \(n=132\). For \(n=12\), the roots are of the form \(u^{2},v^{2},(u+v)^{2}\) with \(u,v\) nonzero and \(u\neq\pm v\); the seven sums \(2u,2v,2(u+v),-2u,-2v,-2(u+v),0\) are all distinct. For \(n=132\), the cubic factors as \((x-16)(x^{2}-6x+25)=0\), so the roots are \(16,\;3+4i,\;3-4i\). Choosing square roots \(4,\;2+i,\;2-i\) gives the seven sums \(8,\;0,\;4+2i,\;-4+2i,\;4-2i,\;-4-2i,\;-8\), which are distinct. Thus both values satisfy the condition. The greatest integer \(n\) is \(132\).
